summary: Trilobit's Atari VCS demo, coded by visy and Ilmarque with graphics and music by Ilmarque, which came second in the demo compo at Stream 2007.
why: A second place at Stream 2007 for a demo on the Atari 2600, one of the most restrictive machines in the scene, with design and direction by visy.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Hacker VBI (code) and Nik-O (music), placed 4th in the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2014. It is a political piece built around the Ukrainian flag and the EU circle of stars.
why: A small, openly political prod from 2014, tagged with a Ukraine theme, that took fourth place in Sundown's old school demo compo.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 invitation to Isterparty 2011, with code, graphics and music by Mermaid and extra art by hedning and Uka: a series of hires pictures and animations, including an Easter bunny and a portrait of an old hedning.
why: Sceners praise the hires graphics and animations, singling out the picture of the old man, and note how much effort went into an invite for such a small party. Later credited as the spark for what became Gubbdata.

quote.text:
Lovely production, such an effort for such a little party :)

I like the rounded edges and supreme hires usage.

summary: Agenda's 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit, which won the Atari XL/XE 16kb Intro compo at Silly Venture 2k14. Code by xeen, graphics by Ooz and Piesiu, music by stRing.
why: It took first place in its category at Silly Venture 2k14, the main Atari 8-bit party.

summary: wAMMA's 4K intro for the Atari VCS, coded by visy and Ilmarque, which placed 5th in the Allround Real Time compo at Outline 2007.
why: A rare 4K demoscene prod on the Atari 2600, with code, graphics and music by Ilmarque on top of visy's engine.

summary: Glance's C64 demo, the finished 100% version of Protogeo released on the last day of 2020, nearly a decade after the 80% version shown at X. It fits on one disk side and ends on a filled vector cube.
why: Sceners single out the closing cube, a 50fps filled vector with fully realtime rotation, long thought out of reach on the C64, along with the chunky effects, cubist artwork and a melancholic soundtrack that holds the whole demo together.

quote.text: Love that real time cube, and all those any pixel any colour parts.  Excellent soundtrack and cubist artwork, too.

summary: Section 31's three-disk-side trackmo for the Commodore Plus/4, which won the demo compo at Árok 2026. Code by Lavina, BSZ, Larry, Mad, Bubis and Murphy, graphics by DLST, Jeva, Harry and Lavina, music by Celticdesign.
why: A first-place compo winner and a large team effort spread over three disk sides. It shows how far the Plus/4 scene pushes the machine, with SID-cart music alongside the TED.

summary: Xenon's C64 demo that won the demo compo at X 2000, with code by WVL and Megabrain, graphics by Oxbow and Spectator, a guest picture by Genius and music by Arman.
why: Sceners praise its flow: seamless, break-less changes between parts and effects synchronised with the music. The scramble upscroller and the moonlit logo reflection get singled out.

quote.text: the upscrambler is one of the most brilliant ideas for a scroller since the DYCP. kudos.

summary: Amstrad CPC demo by Impact, Praline and GPA that won the combined demo/intro compo at ReSeT 2018. Code by AST, graphics by Barjack and music by Tom&Jerry.
why: A first-place winner at ReSeT 2018, with Barjack's detailed pixel art providing the setting for the demo's scrollers.

summary: Desire's 128K Atari XL/XE demo, the second Arsantica, shown at Silly Venture 2k14: a run of effects parts between large hand-drawn pictures, with code by Heaven, Popmilo and Oswald and music by Triace.
why: The coder's notes list a dense set of effects on a stock 130XE: a fractal flight with Koronis Rift-style depth shading, a shaded texture-mapped planet, a 16-shade rotozoomer and realtime radial blur, most aimed at 50 fps.

summary: Camelot's 256-byte Commodore 64 intro, released on Christmas Eve 2013, which won the Mixed category at the Christmas Fun Competition 2013.
why: A compo winner squeezed into 256 bytes, and a seasonal one at that, from a long-running C64 group.

summary: A 16K intro for the ZX Spectrum 128 by Joker, coded and drawn by Dalthon with music by Pator and Zlew. It won the Oldschool Demo compo at Xenium 2021.
why: It took first place in Xenium 2021's Oldschool Demo compo, competing as a 16K intro packed with Shrinkler against full-size entries.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2005, with code and graphics by HCL, more graphics by Jailbird and music by Dane.
why: A lighter-hearted Booze release that sceners rate for its hard-coded parts, Jailbird's pictures and Dane's music. One commenter lists a sprite zoomer over a bitmap among its world-firsts.

quote.text: Hard coded parts with delightful music and gfx.

summary: Offence's 4K intro for the Commodore 64, with code, graphics and music all by Kribust: chunky blocky patterns, scrolling binary digits and a wobbling bar, driven by a hard electronic soundtrack.
why: Sceners call it raw and addictive, praising the banging soundtrack, synced graphics and how long it keeps going without looping. Several admit they left it running for half an hour.

quote.text: This feels like a hammer to the head, but in the most refreshing way possible.

summary: Kpacku's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2014.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions 2014, and tagged as using the Spectrum's multicolour mode for finer colour detail than the stock attribute grid allows.

summary: A short Booze Design demo for the C64, put together largely at Árok 2007 by HCL, with music by Dane and Mitch. It took second place in the demo compo there.
why: Sceners single out the opening double stretcher (a two-layer FPD), which many found beautiful, plus the rotating pig. The common complaint is that it's over too quickly.

quote.text: the double fpd looks so beautiful to me I almost cried :) typical awesomeness from HCL.

summary: Invaders' ZX Spectrum 128K demo, coded by Omega with music by Lamer Pinky, that won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2021. It tells a story set in space.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2021 and a story-led Spectrum demo, with Omega credited for the story as well as code and graphics.

summary: Genesis Project's pirate-themed C64 demo on three disk sides, placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at X 2018. Graphics by Facet, Razorback, Raistlin, hedning and others, with music by Stinsen, Steel and MCH.
why: Sceners single out the sheer amount of pixel work and the coherent pirate theme and flow, and many felt it would have won at most other parties against a less fierce field.
highlights: circle scroller on the light picture

quote.text: Absolutely love this. More than anything is the coherent design / theme and flow. Very well organised and orchestrated <3

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum demo, coded and scored by Gasman, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019. Tagged as karaoke, with on-screen lyrics and messages such as greetings from the UK scene.
why: A runner-up at Revision's Oldskool Demo compo, and a rare Spectrum karaoke demo, with Gasman handling both code and music.

summary: An early Atari 8-bit demo from 1984 by Home Entertainment Centre, credited as a VLM demo. It opens with a text screen announcing that it is being run live, then moves on to coloured symmetrical patterns.
why: A very early piece of Atari 8-bit demo history from 1984. It is worth a look as a record of how computer demonstrations looked before the demoscene's conventions had settled.

summary: Youth Uprising's Game Boy demo, coded and scored by Ferris with graphics by Blake Ridgewell. It placed 2nd in the Combined Demo compo at Pixel Jam 2012.
why: A second place at Pixel Jam 2012 with a strong graphics credit behind it. It's a 4-megabit cartridge production that runs in an endless loop.

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit by LaResistance, coded by Probe with music by Born, which placed second in the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A runner-up at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, that packs its show into a small size limit. The video title gives it as 12K.

summary: A multi-platform Wild compo entry by Moonbase Allstars, running across C64, Linux, MS-DOS and a stack of Nintendo machines from GBC to GameCube, edited together as a video. It placed 3rd in Wild at Revision 2024.
why: Won Outstanding Concept at The Meteoriks 2025, recognised for its idea of turning the old platform wars into a single piece spread over many machines. The source is available.

summary: Agenda's Atari 8-bit demo that came second in the demo compo at Lost Party 2022, with code by tr1x, Koala and xeen, graphics by Piesiu, Ripek and Raphis, and music by Caruso and stRing.
why: A runner-up at Lost Party 2022 from a large Agenda team, with three graphicians credited, so the pictures carry much of the show.
highlights: rainy alley scene with a dog

summary: Lamers' Atari XL/XE demo, second in the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k19, with code by MKM, Ajcek and Szeryf, graphics by Odyn1ec, Blasph and At0m, and music by VLX.
why: A podium finish at Silly Venture, the main party for Atari 8-bit demos, from a large team of coders and graphicians.

summary: Censor Design's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at The Computer Crossroads 1993, with code by Bob, Staiger and Guran, graphics by Dragon and music by Swallow and Danko.
why: Sceners recall it blowing the TCC'93 crowd away and call it the peak of Censor Design's career, their first big compo win after many second and third places. Comments single out its music and effects.

quote.text: This demo blew us all away at the TCC'93 party in Gothenburg.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by g0blinish, with music by Fatal Snipe, that came second in the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2017.
why: A podium finish at Demosplash 2017 for a one-coder Spectrum production. It's tagged as a sequel, so it continues an earlier g0blinish release.
highlights: triangle-tiled shapes in cyan, magenta, yellow

summary: Jumalauta's Game Boy demo, third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2006, shown here running on a real Game Boy Color. Code by Maitotuote, graphics by Äkknäkk and Lesboduo.
why: A podium finish at Assembly's oldskool compo for a handheld demo, with two graphicians credited and a 1 Mbit cartridge to fill.
highlights: filmed on real Game Boy Color

summary: Debris is a 40k intro for the Amstrad CPC by Pulpo Corrosivo, released in August 2022, with code by Toms, music by Tom et Jerry and graphics by Toxic.
why: A recent CPC intro from a small team. There are no compo results or comments to go on, but it drew a warm reception on Pouët.

summary: Nuance's first C64 demo, a one-file dentro that won the Combined Low-End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2011. Code by Bitbreaker, music by Intensity, with realtime hires filled vectors, a twister, a spinning globe and packed animations.
why: Sceners single out how much content is squeezed into a single file, the realtime hires vector routine and the twister. Several also note its cheeky juggling animation, hence the nsfw tag.

quote.text: I would go far to say that it is probably the best one filer I have seen with so much content.

summary: A C64 demo by Horizon, Instinct and Triad that won the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2005, with code by Iopop, Jackasser and Pernod, music by Dalezy and ne7, and graphics by Twoflower.
why: Sceners praise its clean, minimal, coder-led style: the Kefrens-style ice canyon, the line-crunched colour-cycling circles, a moving censor effect and streamed vector animations. Several single out the closing 'The End' part.

quote.text: the kefrens-style canyon is amazing! and the linecrunched color cycle circles are crazy, you get a really weird feeling watching them.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo, coded by sq, Kowalski and psndcj with music by Nik-O and graphics by Diver. It won the Oldskool Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2025.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions 2025 that went on to be nominated for Best Demo in the GOTY ZX Spectrum Awards 2025, and it is on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist.

summary: Speccy.pl's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, coded by Tygrys with graphics by Slayer and CatMan and music by Ziutek. It placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013.
why: A Polish group's entry that held its own in Revision's Oldskool Demo compo and later turned up again at Decrunch 2015, placing 4th in the Twoje Stare Demo compo.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by sibKrew, coded by rook and wbcbz7 with graphics by Robat and music by Nik-O. It placed third in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at CAFe 2019.
why: A podium finish at CAFe 2019 for a demo built on the Spectrum's multicolour mode, with a cast of cartoon characters asking whether the scene can be saved.

summary: A 4K intro for the C64 by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded by Peiselulli, Spider Jerusalem and Street Tuff, with music by Street Tuff. It won the Oldskool intro compo at Revision 2013.
why: Sceners can't believe how much fits into 4K: a smooth plasma, sprite stretchers, effects running into the borders and a soundtrack they rate highly. Several say it looks like a whole demo.

quote.text: I still can't believe that all this fits into 4k. I love the supersmooth plasma, the programmed sound and these all border effects.

summary: Dekadence's C64 demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2004, with code and graphics by BriteLite, 2D and 3D graphics by fragment, music by Agemixer and a loader by SounDemoN.
why: Sceners praised its polish, Agemixer's soundtrack and its timing and flow. Some called it Dekadence's most enjoyable demo so far, though a few found the animations too precalculated.

quote.text: Dekadence's most enjoyable demo (so far) I think. Good stuff.

summary: PRECALCULATED is a ZX Spectrum demo by Skrju that came second in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2015.
why: A podium finish at Chaos Constructions, one of the main Russian-speaking parties for Spectrum work, puts it among the stronger Spectrum demos of 2015.

summary: Mahoney's C64 demo that came second in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2011: a sung Swedish cover tune with the lyrics drawn on screen in big decaying letters, ending with a rotating Android logo.
why: Sceners single out the technical feat of fitting minutes of real-time vocoded vocals into the C64 alongside a soundtrack, plus the 1984 theme. Some found it lo-fi, but many call it one of Mahoney's most inspiring experiments.

quote.text: After this was shown at the party i actually felt no need to watch any of the other contributions.

summary: Benediction's 64K intro for the Amstrad Plus, coded by Eliot with graphics by Pandafox and music by Brink. It placed 8th in the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2016.
why: A Plus-only production from an established CPC group, with a dedicated pixel artist and composer on board. No comments yet, so the compo entry and credits are what there is to go on.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by bfox that won the Low End 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2017 Lite: a Christmas tree drawn from coloured dots.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2017 Lite, showing how much seasonal charm fits into 256 bytes on the Spectrum.

summary: lft's solo C64 demo, with code, graphics and music all by lft, placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013. It runs on lft's own disk loader.
why: Sceners praise its flow and soundtrack, and coders were struck by its loader: Krill called fully decoding a GCR disk block on the fly one of the holy grails of C64 coding, achieved here.

quote.text: I love the this demo , flows very well , good design and great effects , this is why demos are so cool.

summary: Fairlight's two-disk-side C64 demo, a tribute to Last Ninja 3 and a farewell to the Truckstop party venue, which won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2019. Music by Fegolhuzz and Wiklund, graphics by The Sarge.
why: Sceners single out The Sarge's graphics and natural-looking animation, the long credits intro with its lightning effect, and the twister scroller near the end. Even people who usually dislike animation-based demos praise it.

quote.text: I usually don't like animation-based demos, but this one is just so beautiful! Love it!

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by bfox that won the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2017.
why: A compo winner in one of the scene's tightest size limits, taking first place in DiHalt 2017's low-end 256-byte category.

summary: Jumalauta's Game Boy demo that won the 8bit Demo compo at Motorola Inside 2006, filmed here running on an original DMG-001 handheld.
why: A compo winner on the original Game Boy, and a Jumalauta production with a Finnish group's offbeat credits list. Seeing it captured on real hardware shows what the stock screen actually looks like.

summary: Logon System's 1995 Amstrad CPC intro previewing a Shadow Of The Beast conversion: a multi-layered scrolling landscape of clouds, snowy peaks, grass and a stone wall behind a "press fire to play" prompt.
why: Its video is titled as a showcase of parallax scrolling on the CPC, the effect the Amiga original was known for, attempted here on 8-bit hardware.

summary: Fairlight's C64 concept demo by Hollowman, with music by Goto80, that won the demo compo at Floppy 2002: a story told through close-up digitised-style portraits and lines of text.
why: Sceners call it a rare true concept demo, valued for its atmosphere, flow and message rather than effects, and for Goto80's unusual soundtrack that steps away from traditional SID music.

quote.text: Too few people on the scene knows how to do concept demos. True art among tech demos...

summary: Mills' Game Boy Color demo from 2018, with colourful hand-drawn pictures including Homer Simpson eating a doughnut, a smiling Game Boy and a pink "Cute Demo" title screen.
why: A cheerful Game Boy Color demo whose source code is available, with a Simpsons theme running through it.

summary: Megacode's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that placed third in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1997, with code and rendered textures by Exploder and music by Visual.
why: A podium finish at Enlight 1997, one of the big Russian Spectrum parties, and it makes use of the Spectrum's multicolour mode.

summary: Rabenauge and Plush's Commodore PET demo, shown on a CBM 8296 in the video, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2022. Code by Bodo, Krill, Utz and Zed Yago, graphics by Titus, music by Utz.
why: It won its compo at Deadline 2022 and was nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2023, a rare honour for a PET production.

summary: Mahoney's C64 demo that plays an entire compressed vocal sample (Suzanne Vega's "Tom's Diner") through the SID, with on-screen lyrics and a list of the techniques used. Placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2010.
why: Sceners were amazed that a two-minute song could be crammed into a C64 and played back, praising the PC-side encoding and how all three SID voices help rebuild the sample. Krill said it "really used all the tricks in the book".

quote.text: What?! An entire 2-minute song sampled and crammed into this demo?! This is just... awesome!
